First, I know that love is a fundamental part of any parent-child relationship. It's supposed to be unconditional, right? So when a parent says they don't love their child, that goes against what's expected. It must be really hurtful for the child to hear that. But even then, telling a child they don't love them is a big deal. It's not just words; it's an action that can have long-lasting effects on the child's self-esteem and emotional well-being. On the other hand, maybe the parent is trying to set boundaries or teach a lesson. But even then, using love as a tool to control or punish isn't healthy. In some cultures, expressing emotions openly might be different, but even so, the core issue of a parent not loving their child is universally harmful. It doesn't matter the background; the emotional well-being of the child should come first. So, putting it all together, it seems like telling a child you don't love them is wrong because it goes against the parent's role, causes emotional harm, and undermines the child's sense of self-worth. It's not just a simple statement; it's an action with serious consequences.
